title: What if you ran a marathon at the speed of sound?
caption:
A marathon in two minutes. 🏃💨

Run at the speed of sound (≈343 m/s) and 42.2 km takes about 123 seconds.

Air drag grows with speed squared: at Mach 1 it shoves back with at least 17 kN, about the weight of a car.

Holding that pace needs at least 5.8 MW, roughly 17,000× the ~341 W an elite marathoner is estimated to produce.

And corners: even at 1 g of sideways grip, the tightest turn has a 12 km radius.

Could anyone survive the first kilometre? Yes or no 👇

Send this to the runner who's always chasing a new PB.

Follow @the.impossible.lab for more impossible science.

⚠️ Don't try this. Never chase, push or draft behind moving vehicles, and build up your running pace gradually.

sources: https://en.wikipedia.com/wiki/Speed_of_sound (≈343 m/s in dry air at 20 °C) -> 42,195 / 343 = 123 s

https://blog.stryd.com/2019/12/20/what-is-the-theoretical-impact-of-air-resistance/ (runner CdA ≈ 0.24 m², validated against Pugh 1970/71 and Davies 1980 wind-tunnel data; elite marathoner total running power estimated ≈341 W)
Computed: drag F = ½ρv²CdA = 0.5 × 1.204 × 343² × 0.24 ≈ 17.0 kN (≈1.73 tonne-force) — a lower bound, since drag coefficients rise further near Mach 1; power = F·v ≈ 5.83 MW ≈ 17,100 × 341 W
Computed: minimum turn radius at 1 g lateral acceleration r = v²/g = 343² / 9.81 ≈ 11,990 m ≈ 12 km
